question: Does the seven-cell harmonic port intrinsically select the observed (2,1) graphite friction peaks?
assumptions: Periodic orientable honeycomb quotient, connected torus, Euclidean harmonic edge subspace
Reported first-principles Table 2/6 values preserve their respective rigid-layer protocols
Conditional detection window assumes a common proportional force-to-static-shear map and threshold; unverified
physical_mapping: OPEN: static shear and mode drag are not the measured signed kinetic friction; no UD angle-dependent constitutive source specified
sources: Chen et al., PRL 137, 166201 (2026), DOI 10.1103/ly48-b4l2 public abstract
Lebedeva et al., arXiv:2511.01338v1, Tables 2 and 6
baseline: Conventional triangular/moiré geometry and rigid-layer DFT static contrast
result: All tested N=7,13,19 honeycomb torus quotients have b1=2 and uniform source cancellation. The port topology alone cannot single out N=7. Rigid DFT corrugation ratio (2,1)/(3,1) ~12.9 but ideal static shear ratio ~2.08; kinetic force, detection limit and UD residual remain unknown.
next_discriminant: Freeze an independently sourced N-dependent UD constitutive selection and conventional force model, then test signed force and detection limits at paired angles and other moire controls
